title: Tacos de canasta afuera del metro

dialogue.speaker: Carlos
dialogue.spanish: Oye, Valeria, tengo muchísima hambre. ¿Vamos por unos tacos de canasta aquí afuera del metro?
dialogue.english: Hey, Valeria, I'm super hungry. Shall we get some basket tacos right outside the subway?

slang.actualMeaning: Steamed street tacos kept warm in a cloth-lined basket, often sold from a bicycle
slang.example: En la esquina del metro venden tacos de canasta buenísimos.

dialogue.speaker: Valeria
dialogue.spanish: ¡Ay, sí, qué rico! Pero espera, ¿tienes efectivo? Es que el señor de la bicicleta no acepta tarjeta.
dialogue.english: Oh, yes, delicious! But wait, do you have cash? The guy with the bicycle doesn't take cards.

dialogue.speaker: Carlos
dialogue.spanish: Híjole, solo traigo un billete de cincuenta pesos. ¿Cuánto cuestan?
dialogue.english: Shoot, I only have a fifty-peso bill on me. How much do they cost?

slang.actualMeaning: Shoot! / Gosh! / Oh man! (mild Mexican exclamation of surprise)
slang.example: ¡Híjole, se me olvidaron las llaves adentro de la casa!

dialogue.speaker: Valeria
dialogue.spanish: La orden de cinco tacos cuesta cuarenta pesos. Y yo traigo veinte pesos en monedas para dos refrescos.
dialogue.english: An order of five tacos costs forty pesos. And I have twenty pesos in coins for two sodas.

dialogue.speaker: Carlos
dialogue.spanish: ¡Ah, qué chido! Entonces compartimos la orden ahorita y luego en la tarde te pago con transferencia.
dialogue.english: Oh, awesome! Then let's share the order right now and later this afternoon I'll pay you back by bank transfer.

slang.actualMeaning: How awesome / great / cool (classic Mexican slang)
slang.example: ¡Qué chido que pudiste venir a la fiesta!

dialogue.speaker: Valeria
dialogue.spanish: Sale, pide dos de papa con chorizo y tres de frijol. ¡Pero cuidado con la salsa verde que pica un montón!
dialogue.english: Deal, order two potato-and-chorizo ones and three bean ones. But watch out for the green salsa—it's super spicy!

slang.actualMeaning: It's super spicy / has a lot of chili heat
slang.example: No le pongas tanta salsa habanera porque pica un montón.

questions.question: What are Carlos and Valeria trying to figure out outside the subway station ('afuera del metro')?
options: Whether they have enough cash ('efectivo') to buy street tacos and sodas ('refrescos')
Which subway line ('línea del metro') they need to take to get to a restaurant
Where to find an ATM ('cajero') because they lost their wallets
How to cook potato and bean tacos ('tacos de papa y frijol') at home tonight
questions.explanation: Carlos is hungry for tacos de canasta outside the metro, and Valeria checks if they have enough cash ('efectivo') since the bicycle vendor doesn't take cards.

questions.question: How much money does Carlos have on him, and how much does an order of 5 tacos cost?
options: He has a 20-peso bill ('veinte pesos'), and the tacos cost 50 pesos ('cincuenta pesos')
He has a 50-peso bill ('cincuenta pesos'), and the 5 tacos cost 40 pesos ('cuarenta pesos')
He has 100 pesos in coins ('cien pesos'), and the tacos cost 60 pesos ('sesenta pesos')
He has no cash at all, so Valeria pays 40 pesos by card ('con tarjeta')
questions.explanation: Carlos says 'solo traigo un billete de cincuenta pesos' (50-peso bill), and Valeria says 'La orden de cinco tacos cuesta cuarenta pesos' (40 pesos).

questions.question: Which taco fillings does Valeria ask Carlos to order for them to share?
options: Five pork tacos with red salsa ('cinco de carnitas con salsa roja')
Three chicken tacos and two cheese tacos ('tres de pollo y dos de queso')
Two potato-with-chorizo and three bean tacos ('dos de papa con chorizo y tres de frijol')
Four steak tacos and one potato taco ('cuatro de bistec y uno de papa')
questions.explanation: Valeria says: 'Sale, pide dos de papa con chorizo y tres de frijol' (two potato-with-chorizo and three bean tacos).

questions.question: Slang Side Quest: When Carlos says 'Híjole', '¡qué chido!', and Valeria warns that the salsa 'pica un montón', what do those expressions mean?
options: 'Híjole' = shoot/oh man; 'qué chido' = how awesome; 'pica un montón' = it's super spicy
'Híjole' = hurry up; 'qué chido' = how expensive; 'pica un montón' = it costs extra
'Híjole' = excuse me; 'qué chido' = how cold; 'pica un montón' = it's sour
'Híjole' = thank you; 'qué chido' = how small; 'pica un montón' = it's very hot
questions.explanation: In Mexican Spanish, 'híjole' is 'shoot/oh man', 'qué chido' is 'how cool/awesome', and 'pica un montón' means 'it's super spicy!'
